status: Proposals only. Nothing here is scheduled or approved.
costBasis: ESTIMATE throughout. Agent cost scale: R8, a full 6-lane rehearsal, cost about $194 at list price (A-F-01, V1 VERIFIED). Controlled pilot runs cost $0.37-$2.01 per run (A-economics/data/controlled-usage.csv, costUsdListPriceESTIMATE). REL-001 cost about $0.11-$0.16 per correct requirement on fixtures (G-F-08). Human-hours are the owner's or an engineer's time, also ESTIMATE. None of these is a provider bill.

sections.implementation: Work where the evidence is already sufficient to act. It needs engineering, not more research. Each item still states how to confirm the effect after shipping.
sections.research: Questions where the current evidence is SUPPORTED-only, INCONCLUSIVE, NOT TESTED or contradicted across tracks. Decisions should wait for these.

implementation.title: Stop rebuilding the pinned Praxis verifier in every CI run (cache it or use the release binary)
implementation.change: Cache the verifier keyed on its pinned version, or download the attested release binary.
implementation.costEstimate: ESTIMATE: 0.5-1 engineer-day per shared workflow; no agent compute.
implementation.expectedEffect: ESTIMATE: about 604-607 job-minutes across R2-R10 (V1 correction of A-F-13's 688; 7.4-8.0% of step time). The step runs in every Echelon foundations run (about 27% of in-window runs). D-F-09 measured a no-op incremental build at ~4% of clean-build CPU on a similar F# fixture.
implementation.confirmBy: Compare 'Build pinned Praxis verifier' step minutes before and after across the next 2 rehearsals.
implementation.decisionValue: Low risk, measurable. Ship once A2 shows the cache is correct; the binary route needs E-F-09's attestation caveat addressed (verify signer workflow and ref).

implementation.title: Hardened CI template
implementation.change: pipefail on every shell step; !cancelled() instead of if: always(); concurrency with cancel-in-progress set per branch, not per commit; job time caps sized to the measured suite durations; a live test branch per run; explicit permissions blocks; no ${{ inputs.* }} interpolated into run scripts.
implementation.expectedEffect: Removes the two mechanisms behind R6 (85%) and R10 (88%) red or cancelled CI minutes. Excluding those runs, 38% is still red or cancelled, so this is not the whole of the waste.
implementation.confirmBy: Share of red or cancelled job-minutes in the next rehearsal, measured with A's analyze_ci.py.
implementation.decisionValue: High. Two tracks agree on the cause, from independent data (matrix X-08).

implementation.title: Close cheap Praxis completion gaps
basis: E-F-12 (all VERIFIED by E; V2 pending)
implementation.change: Reject evidence paths outside the repository and record a digest and commit for each evidence file. Make the claim guard check the tracked event log. Detect a queue.json status that has no transition. Refuse an authority that requires nothing. Show 'self-declared' or 'unattested' wherever 'complete' or 'verified' is displayed.
implementation.expectedEffect: The bypass cases NX-1, NX-2b, NX-7 and NX-9 become refused. Re-run E's bypass-cases.sh to confirm.
implementation.confirmBy: E-security/scripts/bypass-cases.sh plus the gate-v319 regression on the new release.
implementation.decisionValue: High for integrity. Wait for V2 to independently confirm E-F-01 before announcing anything externally.

implementation.title: Add E's bypass matrix and the REL-001 gate script to Praxis release CI
implementation.change: Run gate-v319 plus E-X02 as release-blocking tests.
implementation.expectedEffect: Prevents regression of the controls that work today.
implementation.confirmBy: Tests present and blocking in Praxis release workflow.

implementation.title: Branch protection, CODEOWNERS and agent credential separation on governance-critical repositories
implementation.change: Owner action: protect main on praxis, Indy-init, the rehearsal repositories and acceptance stores; add CODEOWNERS for workflows and ros.json; give agents a non-admin credential that is distinct from the owner's login.
implementation.expectedEffect: Prerequisite for ADR-S03. It does not fix E-F-02 by itself.
implementation.confirmBy: list_branches shows protected=true; a test push by the agent credential to a protected branch is refused (performed by the owner, not by an agent).
implementation.decisionValue: High. Note that rulesets were unreadable here, so first check whether protection already exists at org level.

implementation.title: Telemetry fixes: execution clock, block reasons and CI waits
implementation.change: Start time.wall_ms at transcript start; require a timestamped block reason; record CI waits and owner requests and answers as events.
implementation.expectedEffect: Makes approval and CI wait measurable. Several research items below (FX-04, FX-06) need this first.
implementation.confirmBy: blocked_ms non-zero and approval events present in the next rehearsal.
implementation.decisionValue: Enabling. Without it, the next sprint will hit the same NOT TESTED wall (matrix X-22).

implementation.title: Supply-chain baseline: vulnerability scan step and NuGet lock files
implementation.change: Add one dependency-vulnerability step to the shared foundations-verify workflow, which 12 repositories already call; enable RestorePackagesWithLockFile; pin curl|sh installers to a release tag and verify attestation.
implementation.decisionValue: Medium. Hygiene; independent of the rehearsal outcome.

implementation.title: Compact structured notifications to the coordinator (ADR-S05 option 1)
implementation.change: Sub-agents report a fixed small status record (work item, SHA, gate result, blocking issue) instead of transcripts or long tool output.
implementation.expectedEffect: Slower coordinator context growth, without the restart risk that FX-04 tests.
implementation.confirmBy: Coordinator mean context per request in the next rehearsal (R8 baseline 416,786).

implementation.title: Affected-project test selection and kept build outputs in agent and CI loops
basis: D-F-09, D-F-10, D-F-11 (SUPPORTED; preregistered confirmatory, one fixture)
implementation.change: Keep build outputs between runs; run only the affected test projects in the inner loop and full suites at merge or gate; avoid public-surface edits to root projects where possible, because they rebuild the cone (D-F-10).
implementation.costEstimate: ESTIMATE: 1-3 engineer-days for a selection script plus CI wiring.
implementation.expectedEffect: ESTIMATE: inner-loop verification CPU down to ~4-15% of full (D-F-11 0.037; whole-step SPR-D-07 0.143, n=4). Selection safety (missed regressions) is NOT TESTED.
implementation.confirmBy: Track build/test CPU per agent execution and escaped-defect count before and after.
implementation.decisionValue: Medium. Cost evidence is solid for one fixture, but the safety side is unmeasured, so keep full suites at the gate.

research.title: Does a pre-T0 governance dry run catch the in-window governance defects?
research.hypothesis: A stub-implementation dry run of the exact frozen package detects at least 70% of the governance-artefact defects that B-F-03 records for R8, R9, R10 and Causa before T0.
research.design: Replay. For each of those runs, check out the frozen package and lock as they were at T0; run authorize-implementation, suite preflight, the cycle check and the release gate against a stub; score each recorded B-F-03 event as caught, missed or not applicable. B2-dryrun is doing a version of this now. Extend it to all four runs, with a second coder.
research.costEstimate: ESTIMATE: 4-8 agent-hours of tooling time, about $20-60 list price; 1-2 human-hours for scoring review.
research.decisionValue: Decides ADR-S04. If the catch rate is high, the dry run becomes mandatory. If it is low, the problem is the design of the gates, not their timing.
research.evidenceGap: B-F-03 is SUPPORTED, from one analyst, and no track measured catchability.
research.status: DONE by B2-dryrun (B2-F-01..F-11): 4/8 brief-list blockers caught (robust 2/8), 7/11 extended; semantic defects, the Causa cycle and hosted-CI causes not caught. Follow-up is B3-semantic (generic semantic checks), plus a hosted-CI dry-run variant (B2-F-11, NOT TESTED).

research.title: Merge driver vs per-lane record format for .ros state
research.hypothesis: H1-H3 of SPR-A2-01. Additionally: a per-lane append-only format produces zero .ros conflicts by construction, with no information loss compared with the team's merges.
research.design: Use A2's replay harness on R8 and R10. Add an arm that rewrites history into a per-lane event layout and replays it.
research.costEstimate: ESTIMATE: 1-2 engineer-days for the format arm; replay compute is negligible.
research.decisionValue: Chooses between ADR-S02 option 1 and option 2.
research.evidenceGap: Prototype results pending; GitHub server-side merges cannot run drivers.
research.notes: DECISION-LOG D-019: a .ros driver cannot remove R8's 4 application-code branch merges (V1).

research.title: Does requirements-compiler verify-plan catch the fabricated acceptance bundle?
research.hypothesis: verify-plan, like the ledger verifier, accepts candidate-produced fabricated result files.
research.design: Extend E's indy_fabricated_acceptance.py to also fabricate the result files verify-plan reads; run rehearsal-005's full acceptance.sh locally.
research.decisionValue: Sets the severity of E-F-02 for R5's actual pipeline, and therefore the urgency of ADR-S03.
research.evidenceGap: E-F-02 limitation: verify-plan was not tested.

research.title: Coordinator context cap: controlled comparison
research.hypothesis: A coordinator that refreshes from a structured checkpoint whenever context exceeds about 200k tokens uses fewer total tokens than an uncapped coordinator on the same scope, with no increase in coordination errors.
research.design: Fixed scope: a reduced Causa slice of 10-15 work items across 3 lanes. 2 arms (capped vs uncapped) × n=3 or more; the same task-agent brief. Measure total tokens, coordinator tokens, coordination errors (wrong merge, lost change request, duplicate dispatch) and wall time. Preregister. Sample size: D-F-08 suggests about 5 paired blocks if effects resemble VAC-001; whole-run variance is unobserved, so plan n=6 per arm and treat as exploratory below that.
research.costEstimate: ESTIMATE: about $25-60 per run (scaled from R8's coordinator plus task agents at reduced scope) × 6 runs = $150-360; 1 day of human analysis.
research.decisionValue: Decides ADR-S05. Resolves the X-12 tension between A-F-03 and VAC-001's continuity result.
research.evidenceGap: A's saving is an ESTIMATE; VAC-001 points the other way for implementers.

research.title: Process-protocol overhead on tasks without a ceiling effect
research.hypothesis: On a task where the plain arm fails at least 20% of requirements, a construction protocol improves acceptance enough to offset its +47-93% token overhead.
research.design: Pick or build a harder fixture (pilot until the plain arm is below 80% acceptance). 3 arms (plain, protocol, mechanical-first), n=8 per arm, chosen from a power calculation on the CONSTRUCT-008 variance. Use final output tokens, not streaming lower bounds (V1 G-F-08 caveat). Grade acceptance with an independent verifier, not the agent's own.
research.costEstimate: ESTIMATE: about $1-3 per run × 24 = $25-75, plus fixture-building time of 1-2 days.
research.decisionValue: Decides whether Echelon process guidance is net-negative (A-F-16, G-F-08) or only ceiling-masked. Also shapes the commercial claim in outline 3.
dependsOn: D2-agent-experiment (governed vs minimal, n=4 per arm, exploratory): use its variance for sizing
research.evidenceGap: n=3 pilots; every published comparison sits at the ceiling (all arms 39/39 or 96/96).

research.title: Agent count vs fixed scope
research.hypothesis: With scope held fixed, going from 1 to 3 to 6 lanes reduces wall time sublinearly and raises total tokens through coordination and conflicts.
research.design: The same reduced scope as FX-04, with 1, 3 and 6 lanes, n=2-3 each. Measure tokens, wall time, conflicts and defects.
research.decisionValue: Topology choice for future rehearsals; A-F-17 is NOT TESTED.
research.evidenceGap: No dataset varies agent count at fixed scope.

research.title: Review timing: early-and-after-every-fix vs end-of-run
research.hypothesis: Independent review at the first release candidate and after every fix round leaves fewer open defects at the deadline than a single review near the end.
research.design: Seeded-defect fixture, 2 arms, n=4 or more; reviewers spawned from a separate session with no implementer context.
research.decisionValue: B-F-11 is SUPPORTED and observational. This would justify making review timing a rule.
research.evidenceGap: No controlled comparison of review timing.

research.title: Inter-rater reliability of the B event corpus
research.hypothesis: A second coder assigns the same root-cause code to at least 80% of B's 135 events (Cohen's kappa ≥ 0.7).
research.design: A blinded second coder, human or a separate agent with no access to B's labels, codes events from the same source lines using taxonomy.json.
research.decisionValue: Needed before B-F-03's prevalence counts or DS-B-EVENTS are cited externally.

research.title: Reconcile the sprint's own measurement disagreements
research.hypothesis: The differences between A, B, V1 and A2 in merge counts (X-02, X-03), in Actions run counts (A 4,633 vs B 3,222, different repository sets) and in R8 ledger counts (49 vs 48) are explained by window and ref definitions.
research.design: One script that applies a single window and ref-set definition to both Actions fetches and all three merge replays, and reports the residuals.
research.decisionValue: Prevents publishing inconsistent counts. A prerequisite for outline 2.

research.title: Do buyers value an independent, attested definition of done?
research.hypothesis: Engineering leaders at 10 or more target firms rank independent completion verification among their top 3 AI-governance needs and state willingness to pay.
research.design: Structured interviews (owner-led) plus a review of supply-chain attestation tooling (SLSA, in-toto), which G did not survey.
research.decisionValue: G-F-09 is INCONCLUSIVE, inferred from absence on marketing pages. This decides whether outline 3's positioning is worth pursuing.

research.title: Range qualification end to end
research.hypothesis: With a trusted Registry key, Conditor's attestedQualification admits a signed set range without a Conditor release and refuses an unsigned or tampered set.
research.design: Scratch key, scratch Registry set, local Conditor build; positive and negative cases (unsigned, wrong key, tampered digest).
research.decisionValue: ADR-S01 assumes this code path works; it has only been read (C-F-04).

research.title: Chain-level replication of the VAC-001 continuity effect
research.hypothesis: Agent continuity's cost advantage (about -40%) holds with 6 or more independent chains per arm.
research.design: Rerun VAC-001 arms A and B with more chains and analyse at chain level (D's unit-of-independence note). D-F-08: about 5 blocks for B vs A and DR vs D at the observed effects (lower bounds); plan 6+ independent chains per arm.
research.decisionValue: VAC-001 is one of the few positive results (G-F-08) and it bears on ADR-S05. Its current CI overstates replication precision.
research.evidenceGap: 3 chains (B vs A); 1 chain for DR vs D.

research.title: Live vs fake provider detection
research.hypothesis: Running live-provider checks from the first write detects provider-behaviour defects at least one review round earlier than fakes alone.
research.design: Seeded provider-divergence fixture (rate limit, 422, moved head), with arms using fakes only vs fakes plus a live sandbox repository.
research.decisionValue: B-F-06 is observational, with no comparison run after R2.
research.evidenceGap: No run without live checks after R2.
